name: Aliased
description: A name on each row with the aliases it was also known by, unique across the table: no two rows hold one name, as a name or an alias, in its normalized form. normalize lower, the default, reads a name with its case and its runs of white space ignored; slug reads only its letters and digits, in lower case. A create gives the name. rename keeps the old name as an alias; addAlias and removeAlias keep the others; resolve, on the table, finds the row a name or an alias names. A name another row holds is refused with that row's key, the veto name_taken. A delete frees the row's names, and a removed alias frees its own. The behaviors' core alone implements it, on a table; no engine type composes it.

normalize.description: How two names are read as one: lower, the default, compares them in lower case with the white space at their ends dropped and each run of it within one space; slug compares only their letters and digits, in lower case, each run of anything else one hyphen.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The row's name, as a create or a rename gave it: no other row holds it, as a name or an alias, in its normalized form.

tables.name: aliases
tables.description: The row's aliases, one per normalized form: a name it was renamed from, or one addAlias gave it. A removeAlias deletes its row, and a merge moves the row merged away's to the row that stays.

fields.name: normalized
fields.description: The alias in its normalized form, which keys it within its row.

fields.name: alias
fields.description: The alias as it was given.

tables.name: names
tables.description: On a table, one row per name a row holds, as its name or an alias, kept for the table as a whole and keyed by its normalized form, so the database holds each unique: a create or a rename that takes a name another row holds finds its row here. A removed alias and a deleted row's names delete theirs.

fields.name: normalized
fields.description: The name in its normalized form.

fields.name: holder
fields.description: The key of the row that holds the name, as its name or an alias.

operations.name: rename
operations.description: Gives the row a new name, keeping the old one as an alias. A name the row holds as an alias becomes its name; one only its case or spacing changes leaves the aliases as they are. A name another row holds is refused, the veto name_taken. The name the row has is answered unchanged.

alias.description: The old name, kept as an alias; absent when the rename kept none.

unchanged.description: True when the row had the name already, so nothing was written; absent otherwise.

operations.name: addAlias
operations.description: Adds an alias the row is also known by. A name another row holds is refused, the veto name_taken; one the row holds already, as its name or an alias, is answered unchanged.

unchanged.description: True when the row held the alias already, so nothing was written; absent otherwise.

operations.name: removeAlias
operations.description: Removes one of the row's aliases, freeing it for any row. The row's name is refused, the veto is_name: a rename gives the row another first. An alias the row does not hold is answered unchanged.

alias.description: The alias to remove, in any form that normalizes to it.
The alias removed, as it was given when added; the one asked for when the row held none.

unchanged.description: True when the row held no such alias, so nothing was written; absent otherwise.

operations.name: resolve
operations.description: Finds the row whose name or alias a name names, in its normalized form: a read of the table as a whole that writes nothing.

name.description: The name or alias to find.

row.description: The row that holds the name; null when none does.

key.description: The row's key, in its wire form.

alias.description: True when the name found is one of the row's aliases, false when it is its name.

vetoes.description: A create, a rename or an addAlias of a name another row holds, as its name or an alias, in its normalized form; details give the name, its normalized form and the key of the row that holds it (holder).
removeAlias of the row's name, which is no alias: a rename gives the row another name first; details give the name.
